- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.27) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce the peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to sentiment-driven momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — adjust downward only if sentiment persists for 3+ days.
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative mid-period, model should slow down or reverse direction by day 5–7 to avoid lagged reactions.
- If forecast shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of overcorrection), reduce the magnitude of correction by 10–15% to prevent over-adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in 2+ consecutive days, reduce next-day forecast by 5–8% to account for momentum decay.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.26) and price is near historical mean, avoid large swings — forecast should be within ±2% of 14-day moving average.
- If forecast spikes after a negative sentiment day, reduce the spike by 10–15% to avoid sentiment-driven overcorrection.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, forecast should not exceed 1.5x the 30-day average unless accompanied by strong technical confirmation.
